title: Sepsis, severe sepsis, septic shock, urosepsis and bacteremia
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the sepsis, severe sepsis or septic shock only (not the local infection or the organ dysfunction). If none applies, choose 'no code'.
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/20/2026
Reason for Admission: Severe pneumonia and septic shock.

Vitals:
BP: 110/70 mmHg
HR: 88 bpm
Temp: 98.6 F
SpO2: 95% on room air
Weight: 175 lbs

Recent Labs:
WBC: 14.2 x 10^9/L
Lactate: 4.2 mmol/L (on admission)
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
Hemoglobin: 13.2 g/dL

Review of Systems:
The patient reports cough and shortness of breath. He denies chest pain, abdominal pain, or neurological deficits. He denies recent travel or known exposure to sick contacts.

Social History:
The patient resides in a private home with his wife. He retired ten years ago. He denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History:
Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes. No history of sudden cardiac death in the immediate family.

Hospital Course:
The patient is an 86-year-old male who presented to the emergency department with productive cough, fever, and altered mental status. Initial evaluation revealed signs of severe pneumonia. The patient quickly progressed to septic shock, requiring the initiation of vasopressor support to maintain adequate mean arterial pressure. Broad-spectrum antibiotics were administered promptly. Cultures were obtained, but no specific organism grew in the blood or sputum samples. The patient remained on vasopressors for several days. With aggressive fluid resuscitation and antibiotic therapy, his hemodynamic status stabilized, and he was successfully weaned off all vasopressors. His oxygen requirements decreased, and his mental status improved significantly over the course of the stay. He remained stable for the final 48 hours of admission and is now ready for transition to home care.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Sepsis due to pneumonia
Septic shock

Discharge Medications:
Amoxicillin 500mg TID
Acetaminophen 650mg every 6 hours as needed for fever
Multivitamin daily

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with his primary care physician in one week for a routine check-up and to monitor his recovery from the septic shock.

Electronically signed, 
P. O'Brien, MD
05/20/2026
explanations: Septic shock is severe sepsis with circulatory failure: A41.9 plus R65.21.

distractors.why: Septic shock is documented: R65.21, not R65.20.

style.document: Write a hospital discharge summary with sections: Admission Date, Discharge Date, Reason for Admission, Hospital Course, Discharge Diagnoses, Discharge Medications, Follow-up. It is the inpatient record of this hospital stay, not an office note.
